clue.text: Attempt a portion of beef for two

indicators.note: a portion of the phrase beef for two is taken, so the letters run across its words

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a serving of beef big enough for two diners.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is a try or exertion made at something, which is the meaning of the noun here.

clue.text: Resident abroad subsequently heading off round Pennsylvania

indicators.note: round means the shortened word goes around the state's abbreviation
heading off means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: next means subsequently or afterwards
PA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: Someone living overseas later sets off on a tour of Pennsylvania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' cuts NEXT to EXT, and 'round' wraps it round PA: EX-PA-T.
explanation.definitionFit: An expatriate is a person living outside their native country.

clue.text: Genuine article installed by company as warning device

indicators.note: installed by means placed within, so the firm holds the other pieces

parts.note: a firm is a company
real means genuine
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A firm fits the real thing as a safety alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire alarm is a bell or siren that alerts people to a blaze.

clue.text: Supremes singer, one entertaining trendy musician

indicators.note: entertaining in the sense of hosting, holding a guest within

parts.note: Diana Ross was lead singer of the Supremes, the Motown group
I is the Roman numeral one
in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: A Motown star hosts a fashionable composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian composer of The Barber of Seville.

clue.text: Helpful type, like close relative

parts.note: like in the sense 'in the manner of' gives as
a sister is a close family relative

explanation.surface: A helpful person is described as being like a close family member.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who assists or aids others is a helpful type of person.

clue.text: Teach-sir dot com revolutionised the education system

indicators.note: revolutionised means turned upside down, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An online venture called teach-sir dot com transformed schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Socratic method is a teaching approach based on questioning, named after the Greek philosopher.

clue.text: One part of the Bible- Old Testament book, actually

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
NT is short for the New Testament
Ruth is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Scripture readings combine a New Testament section with an Old Testament book.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means really or in fact, just as actually does.

clue.text: Giant container not quite big enough for storing it

indicators.note: storing means holding inside, so the shortened container keeps the word it within
not quite means the word falls one letter short at its end

parts.note: a tank is a container for liquid

explanation.surface: A huge receptacle proves slightly too small to keep something in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' cuts TANK to TAN, and 'for storing' puts IT inside: T-IT-AN; 'big enough' supports the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person or thing of enormous size, after the giant gods of Greek myth.

clue.text: More than one scripture teacher N makes sound R S improvements?

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject covering scripture
a master is a schoolteacher; 'More than one' asks for the plural

explanation.surface: Several religious studies teachers seem to be getting better at acoustics.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education in British schools; the stray N and R S are print debris around the definition 'makes sound improvements'.
explanation.definitionFit: Remastering an old recording improves its audio quality.

clue.text: String of high grades given to TV newslady, honest

parts.note: a run of top marks is a series of straight As
Kate Adie is a well-known BBC television news reporter

explanation.surface: A newsreader with a string of top marks is called upright.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate Adie is a British TV journalist, famous as the BBC's chief news correspondent.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means thoroughly honest and upright, like a perfectly straight tool.

clue.text: Patricia's terribly dependent on others

indicators.note: terribly suggests the name is badly mangled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Patricia is criticised for leaning too heavily on other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges all nine letters of PATRICIAS, the possessive S included.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off a host, so parasitic behaviour relies on others for support.

clue.text: Art of piano playing?

parts.note: read 'Art' as a man's name: the jazz pianist whose first name was Art, famous for his keyboard playing

explanation.surface: A question about the craft of playing the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: Art Tatum was a celebrated American jazz pianist; 'Art' is his first name, not the noun for skill.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the jazz pianist Art, a virtuoso of piano playing.

clue.text: Worker returns carrying garment for empress

indicators.note: carrying means the reversed worker holds the garment within it
returns means the worker's word comes back the other way, read backwards

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's usual worker insect
a sari is a garment worn in South Asia

explanation.surface: A labourer comes back bearing clothing fit for an empress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns ANT into TNA, and 'carrying' puts SARI inside: T-SARI-NA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a tsar, the title of a Russian empress.

clue.text: Ex-student starts to make notes, getting in usual mess

indicators.note: getting in means those opening letters go inside the jumbled word
mess signals that the word usual is muddled into a new order
starts to make and notes means the opening letters of those two words are taken

explanation.surface: A former pupil begins jotting things down while sorting the usual clutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' rearranges USUAL to AL U US, and 'getting in' puts MN (the first letters of make and notes) inside: ALU-MN-US.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a graduate or former pupil of a school or college.

clue.text: Taking risks, as a pyromaniac may be?

explanation.surface: A firebug's habit is likened to living dangerously.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means courting danger, while literally someone obsessed with fire would be toying with flames.

clue.text: Musical piece making clergyman bitter?

parts.note: a pastor is a minister or clergyman
bitter is a type of British beer, an ale

explanation.surface: Asking whether a composition makes a vicar resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' looks like an adjective but is the British pub beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastorale is a composition evoking rural life, a pastoral instrumental work.

clue.text: Religious woman I first invited out is D E overwhelmed

indicators.note: first means the I goes at the front of the other pieces

parts.note: a nun is a woman in a religious order
dated means took out on a date

explanation.surface: A man confesses to dating a nun and feeling swamped.
explanation.definitionFit: Inundated means flooded or swamped, as with letters or requests.

clue.text: Eddie Cochran's case of seasonal affective disorder?

definitions.text: Eddie Cochran's case of seasonal affective disorder?

parts.words: Eddie Cochran's case of seasonal affective disorder
parts.note: seasonal affective disorder is low mood tied to a season; Eddie Cochran's 1958 rock and roll hit is about feeling down during the hot months

explanation.surface: A rock and roll singer is diagnosed with a seasonal low mood.
explanation.walkthrough: Seasonal affective disorder is usually winter gloom; Cochran's song turns it to the hot months, with 'blues' as low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Cochran's song describes being miserable in the warm season, a seasonal depression.

clue.text: Football team leaping over net

indicators.note: leaping suggests the letters jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: A side's player jumps clear of the goal net.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is an English Premier League football club from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a professional football club, a team playing in Liverpool.

clue.text: Nationality is given during birth, possibly

indicators.note: given during means placed inside the jumbled word
possibly suggests the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A person's citizenship is assigned when they are born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges BIRTH to BRITH, and 'given during' puts IS inside: BRIT-IS-H.
explanation.definitionFit: British is the nationality of citizens of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Bully journalists at work

parts.note: op is short for operating or in operation, as in 'in op', meaning working
the press is the collective name for journalists

explanation.surface: Reporters are accused of intimidation while on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone is to oppress or tyrannise them, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Pen used by American writer

explanation.surface: An enclosure is used by a US author.
explanation.walkthrough: Ezra Pound was an American modernist poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound is an animal enclosure; Ezra Pound was an American poet.

clue.text: Editor's repaired valves

indicators.note: repaired suggests the parts are put back together differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor's broken radio valves have been fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' rearranges EDITORS, the possessive S included.
explanation.definitionFit: A triode is a three-electrode vacuum tube, the kind of thermionic valve used in old radios.

clue.text: Tomatoes can be a bit off

explanation.surface: A remark that tomatoes sometimes go bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomatoes are full of pips; the word also means slightly unwell or disreputable.

clue.text: Grown-up: one having endlessly boring time

parts.note: one as the article a

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: boring means dull

explanation.surface: A mature person is said to lead a tedious life.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up is a fully developed person, someone of mature age.

clue.text: Shaw character idle, do you say?

indicators.note: do you say asks how the phrase is spoken, signalling a word that sounds the same

parts.note: someone idle does little

explanation.surface: Asking whether a character from Shaw is lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza Doolittle is the flower girl in Shaw's Pygmalion; her surname is said like 'do little'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza and her father Alfred are characters in George Bernard Shaw's play Pygmalion.

clue.text: Risk way to bring about appeasement

explanation.surface: Taking a gamble is offered as the route to calming tempers.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as END ANGER: to put a stop to someone's rage is the way to appease them.
explanation.definitionFit: To risk something is to imperil it; read as two words, it means stopping fury, which pacifies.

clue.text: Reluctant to pen unconventional yarn

indicators.note: to pen means to enclose, so one word is put inside another

parts.note: shy means reluctant or wary
odd means unconventional or strange

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates to write an offbeat story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like a story, but it is the definition: shoddy is a cheap yarn made from recycled wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy is a cheap wool fibre spun from shredded rags, a kind of recycled thread.
